title: Chapter 3252 Preventative Measures
content:
Finally, the time of the gathering the Jade Queen had promised to host had arrived. There was a splendid feast. There was beautiful music and exquisitely skilled dancers; a sorcerer who put on a stunning display, turning the great hall of the Jade Palace into a flowing gallery of breathtaking spectacles for a short while. There was even a troupe of Awakened Beasts taught how to perform astonishing tricks and a jester skillful in both physical comedy and biting remarks.

...The jester ended up embedded in a wall after one of his jokes seemed to offend the Jade Queen, who had been laughing and giggling at his antics perfectly well up to that point.

Luckily, the jester was a Transcendent Devil, and one famous for being both hardy and tenacious at that — so he survived the queen's ire with only a few broken bones.

After the feast, the challengers of the Nightmare gathered in a council room. There were supposed to be four of them — but now, unexpectedly, there were five. Smile of Heaven joined the four Supremes, looking around hesitantly.

The Jade Queen herself, however, was absent. Cassie remarked that she would invite her after they discussed a few matters on their own.

Sitting down, Sunny looked around the sprawling table carved from pristine white jade.

There was Sunny himself, the Lord of Shadows. Nephis, Changing Star of the Immortal Flame clan. Her mother, Smile of Heaven — the first human in history to receive a True Name in the First Nightmare, even if she was a mere Transcendent now. There was Mordret, the King of Nothing. And, of course, there was Cassie... Song of the Fallen, the Oracle of Thetis.

Sunny knew how he had spent the countless years of this Nightmare. He knew what Nephis had done, as well. Both of them were far more powerful now than they had been before entering the Seed — incomparably so, even. The same could be said about Mordret and Cassie, even if he was not sure of the extent their power had grown.

Mordret had spent most of the Nightmare trying to engineer his own Unmaking. He seemed to have succeeded, at least to a degree, then spent centuries observing the Demon of Desire and the Demon of Destiny. It was difficult to say what thoughts churned behind his mirror-like eyes, but Sunny felt that the King of Nothing had approached the threshold of goodhood, as well.

As for Cassie...

Sunny glanced at her, feeling uneasy. Cassie had grown more powerful, without a doubt. Her Domain seemed to have expanded by quite a lot — of course, it had. How could it be the same? It was composed of memories, after all. Having accumulated thousands of years of memories within the Nightmare, Cassie naturally had far more to remember. The countless people she met... among those, there were surely those who were worth summoning.

In fact, if Sunny knew Cassie at all, she must have sought out specific beings on purpose, simply because they could be of great help as manifested memories.

With her Domain having grown, she could manifest more memories and sustain them for longer, as well.

But that was not the most profound change Cassie had undergone.

What had truly changed her was her newly regained right eye, which had once belonged to Weaver, but was a part of her now. The same eye the Vile Thieving Bird had stolen, but then dropped from its beak. The same eye that had driven that loathsome Terror mad and infected its soul with Corruption.

In the description of the Drop of Ichor Sunny had consumed, the Spell mentioned that there was a reflection of the -unknown- forever frozen in the depths of Weaver's pupil. It was seeing that reflection that had tainted the Thieving Bird's soul with Corruption and shattered its mind. The Drop of Ichor was long gone, so Sunny could not be sure what that unknown reflection was. But given that he knew that Weaver had entered the Void once, he felt quite confident that it was the reflection of the Void... or of a particular being Weaver had beheld there.

No wonder even a Sacred Terror was instantly Corrupted.

What about Cassie, then? Why had she not succumbed to Corruption the moment she approached Weaver's eye, let alone later, when it became a part of her body?

The answer was simple.

It was because of her Flaw.

Cassie could not see — her blindness was not mundane in nature, but mystical and absolute — and that was why the reflection frozen in the depths of Weaver's pupil had no power over her.

That did not mean that assimilating the eye of the Demon of Fate had not affected her in a dire manner.

The enchantment of Weaver's Mask that allowed its wearer to gaze upon the infinite — and harrowing in its infinity — tapestry of fate was called [Where is my eye?]. From that, one could somewhat infer that Weaver had created that enchantment to make up for losing an eye and regain their ability to see fate, or at least do so easily. Therefore... one could also suppose that the ability Weaver had lost because of the Vile Thieving Bird remained contained within the stolen eye.

And by making Weaver's eye her own, Cassie gained a form of that ability as well.

She had always been sensitive to fate, receiving glimpses of the absolute knowledge contained within its twisting strings in the form of prophetic visions. But once the daemon's eye rooted itself in her empty eye socket, Cassie found herself gazing at the tapestry of fate directly — as much of it as she could perceive as a Supreme, at least.

As she had described it to Sunny, that was her second Unmaking.

The terrible visage of the tapestry of fate shattered her sanity, plunging her into madness and incomprehension. Torrents of fragmented visions and an endless sea of knowledge flowed into her mind, tearing it apart. She became lost in the boundless expanse of intertwined fates, unable to distinguish reality from illusion, the present from the past — or from the future.

It took her centuries to slowly teach herself how to close her eyes to fate. It took a long time to learn how to make use of her new eye, as well — and even then, her ability to control what fate showed her remained limited, full of hidden perils.

Nevertheless, Cassie had spent a long time slowly piecing together information about the future of this world — the world contained within a Nightmare.

And in the process, she had also built a kingdom in the realm where Weaver's eye had fallen once.

Thetis.

The peaceful realm where the Nine would be born one day.

Learning of that fact, Sunny could not help but chuckle darkly.

‘So that was where the Vile Thieving Bird dropped the eye...’

It was all bitterly ironic. It was all connected.

Well, of course it was.

Weaver was the Demon of Fate, and yet, they wanted to defy it.

Weaver's eye had fallen in the realm that would one day become known as Thetis — a realm whose people did not worship the gods, but worshiped fate instead. Eventually, nine avatars of fate were born among the people of Thetis.

And those nine Fated champions killed Weaver... they destroyed the world.

Or rather, they almost did — they would have, if not for Weaver's final, most grandiose scheme.

...And now, thousands of years later, Sunny — both an heir of Weaver and one of the Fated — had to deal with the consequences of what fate, the Demon of Fate, and fate's chosen had done.

While Cassie, the person responsible for breaking fate, had come to inherit Weaver's stolen eye.

‘Quite a conundrum.'

In any case, at the end of it all, it was good news for Sunny and the other challengers. Even if it took thousands of years, they had finally found each other. They had endured the Unmaking and recovered from its dreadful strain. They had avoided the many perils of the Fifth Nightmare — staying alive, if not unscathed — and regained themselves.

And now that they were ready to face the final challenge of the Nightmare, Cassie was there, having spent centuries investigating, gathering clues, and trying to glimpse the surest way... perhaps the only way... for them to win.

As the five of them looked at each other, an uneasy silence settled over the chamber. Eventually, it was Cassie who broke it.

“I guess all of you are wondering what the central conflict of that Nightmare is."

Sunny chuckled, while Nephis and Mordret just looked at her without saying anything.

Sable, meanwhile, glanced at each of them with a slightly hesitant expression, then cleared her throat and said:

"Yeah... that'd be good to know."

Cassie turned her head slightly, facing her. After a few moments of silence, she spoke in a measured tone:

“The central conflict of this Nightmare revolves around the Nine.”

Then, with a heavy sigh, she leaned back.

“Needless to say, defeating the Nine is far more difficult than it might seem. They are chosen by fate, after all... so, fate is on their side."

Cassie paused for a moment, then added:

“Which is why the best chance of stopping them from destroying the world we have... is preventing the Nine from being born, to begin with. It is eliminating the reason why they turned against the gods."

She straightened and faced them, her expression both calm and solemn.

"So, a few days ago, I declared war on the Empire of War."

Sunny blinked.

"What?"

Nephis tilted her head.

Mordret, meanwhile, spat the water he was trying to drink.

"What?!"

In the silence that followed, Sable's voice resounded:

"Uh, excuse me..."

She looked at each of them in turn, then asked hesitantly:

"...Who the hell are the Nine?"
